subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should OpenClaw add core per-agent spend-budget enforcement, and if so which budget scopes, actions, storage model, and unknown-pricing behavior should become the supported contract?
rationale: The source shows the missing capability is real, but implementing it adds config, provider-routing, admission-control, persisted-state, and operator UX contracts that automation should not choose without maintainer product direction.

options.title: Sponsor a core budget design
options.body: Define the minimal supported core contract for per-agent budget admission, durable reservations/receipts, status and doctor surfaces, then implement behind additive config.

options.title: Keep this as observability only
options.body: Continue improving `usage.status` and `usage.cost` while relying on provider quotas or external proxies for hard spend enforcement.

options.title: Build a generic plugin/API seam first
options.body: Expose a pre-dispatch policy hook so external budget systems can enforce spend without adding OpenClaw-owned budget policy yet.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core budget design
recommendation.body: Define the minimal supported core contract for per-agent budget admission, durable reservations/receipts, status and doctor surfaces, then implement behind additive config.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly tied to current usage RPC/source provenance and adjacent merged usage-cost work.
